findings.text: cgroup_show_path is a globally visible helper that renders a namespace relative filesystem path for a kernfs node into a sequential output channel. It is described here as an interface boundary for path display, not as internal logic.

The taskset cursor exposes two visible routines that start and advance iteration over tasks selected for migration. Callers obtain a task pointer and an associated destination subsystem state pointer, with a null task marking exhaustion.

of_peak is a visible accessor that yields the peak tracking record held in the private context of an open kernfs file. It lets other control file logic reach that record without knowing the container layout.

Iteration over per cgroup subsystem states uses read copy update dereference that is validated against the main cgroup mutex. The contract is that a caller holds that mutex or otherwise satisfies the read copy update check while walking the subsystem table, and skips empty slots.

The initial css set object starts with a single reference and points its domain member at itself. It carries empty list anchors for ordinary tasks, migration tasks, dying tasks, iterators, threaded sets, group links and migration nodes, and points its default group member at the default hierarchy root so early boot lookups remain safe.
The global count of css sets starts at one to account for the initial set alone. It represents the population baseline before any further sets are created.
The width used for sizing the css set hash table is seven bits. Implementations must size that table as two raised to seven entries.

Root teardown proceeds through tracing and draining offline members of the default hierarchy, then emits a lifetime offline notification, rebinds subsystems attached to the dying root back to the default hierarchy, releases cset linkage records, removes the root from the global root list with a decrement of the root population, clears dynamic modification favor when that feature was never enabled, releases the root identifier, drops the main lock, and finally destroys the kernfs root and frees the root object.

Destruction asserts that no groups remain counted on the root and that the root group has no children. Notification failures are converted and warned once, and subsystem rebind failures trigger warnings rather than aborting teardown.

Link records joining csets to the dying hierarchy root are removed while holding the css set spin lock with interrupts disabled. The surrounding teardown otherwise runs under the main cgroup lock acquired by the drain helper and released before kernfs destruction.

Resolution of the current namespace relative group for a given root requires the caller to already hold the css set lock. Inside, a read copy update read section protects the lookup of the current root cset through the namespace proxy.

The namespace relative lookup is expected to always find a group because the namespace semaphore held by the caller prevents unmount of the root. A one time warning guards the otherwise impossible null result.

Default hierarchy namespace relative resolution normally maps the current namespace root set into the default root. When the calling task has already exited its namespace proxy and that pointer is null, as can happen on certain identifier lookup paths, resolution falls back to the default root itself so all groups stay visible.

A static kernfs syscall operations object is reserved for cgroup filesystem syscalls. The fragment shows only its declaration without populated handlers, indicating that behavior is defined elsewhere or left default in this view.

Path display resolves the caller namespace group for the filesystem root under the css set lock, then renders the kernfs path from the target node relative to that group node into a temporary buffer, escapes blank and newline and backslash characters into the sequential output, and releases the buffer.

Path display fails with out of memory when its temporary buffer cannot be allocated. An oversize indication from the kernfs path helper is translated to a range error, positive lengths denote escaped output success reported as zero, and the buffer is freed on all paths.

Version two mount vocabulary includes a delegation flag spelled nsdelegate that maps to namespace delegation handling, and separately a preference flag spelled favordynmods that maps to dynamic modification preference. Both are valueless boolean options.

Version two mount vocabulary separately includes a memory locality flag spelled memory_localevents and a memory protection flag spelled memory_recursiveprot. Both are valueless booleans governing memory controller event and protection behavior.

Version two mount vocabulary further includes a huge page accounting flag spelled memory_hugetlb_accounting and a process number locality flag spelled pids_localevents. Both are valueless booleans for their respective controllers.

Version two parameter parsing dispatches each recognized mount word to set one corresponding bit in the filesystem context flags and reports success, passes through parser failures, and rejects unknown selections with an invalid argument error.

Root flag application only takes effect when the caller resides in the initial cgroup namespace. Inside that namespace each context bit sets or clears its matching default root flag, with dynamic modification preference routed through a dedicated helper rather than direct assignment.

Option display appends a comma prefixed word for every default root flag currently enabled, covering delegation and modification preference and memory and process number behaviors. Reconfiguration simply reapplies the filesystem context flags to the live default root and reports success.

Filesystem context lifecycle frees the name and release agent strings, drops the namespace reference, releases kernfs context state and the context itself. Tree acquisition marks the default hierarchy visible, holds it live, points the context at the default root, delegates to shared acquisition, and on success applies context flags. Version two and version one operation tables share freeing but bind distinct parsing and tree and reconfiguration handlers.

Context initialization allocates a zeroed context, pins the current cgroup namespace with a reference, selects the operation table by filesystem type, adopts the namespace user namespace for the mount while dropping the previous one, marks the mount global, and presets the modification preference flag when that feature was enabled at build or boot.

Superblock shutdown only initiates killing of a hierarchy root when that root has no children, is not the default root, and its reference is not already dying. It always drops one group reference and delegates final teardown to the kernfs killer.
Filesystem names exposed for mounting are cgroup for version one and cgroup2 for version two. Both allow mounting inside user namespaces.

The cpuset compatibility mount uses the name cpuset and a single boolean word spelled cpuset_v2_mode that selects second generation behavior. Its default release agent is the path /sbin/cpuset_release_agent.

Cpuset parameter parsing recognizes only its version two mode word and sets the matching context flag, passing through parser errors and rejecting anything else as invalid. Its operation table binds shared tree acquisition and freeing with this parser.

Cpuset context setup builds on generic initialization, then overrides the operation table, restricts the subsystem mask to the cpuset controller alone, enables no prefix handling, installs the default agent string, and swaps the filesystem type reference from cpuset to the generic cgroup type while holding and releasing the appropriate module references.

Migration iteration starts at the first cset in the supplied set and with no current task, then walks each cset migration task list in order before advancing to the next cset. When a cset already has a prepared destination, the destination subsystem state is reported, otherwise the source state is reported. Iteration only proceeds when subsystem configuration support is enabled and terminates with null.

Subsystem mask display prints enabled controller names separated by single spaces followed by a newline, emitting nothing when empty. The controllers file shows the effective control mask of the target group while the subtree control file shows its configured subtree mask.

Before mutating delegation state, the current subtree control mask and subtree state mask and domain pointer of every live descendant in preorder are snapshot into corresponding old fields for later finalize or rollback.

Enabling delegation is vetted so that an empty enable set always passes, the target domain must be valid, mixable groups bypass further checks, domain controllers are refused inside thread roots or threaded groups with EOPNOTSUPP, threaded controllers are allowed inside actual or prospective thread roots and threaded groups, and any group currently holding tasks refuses new enables with EBUSY to avoid competition between tasks and children.

Subtree control updates parse a space separated list of controller names each prefixed to enable or disable, ignoring empty tokens and rejecting unknown names or missing signs. After locking the live group, already satisfied enables or disables are filtered out, enables require presence in the effective control mask, disables require absence from every live child subtree mask, vetting must pass, then control is saved, masks updated, applied and finalized, with the kernfs node activated only on success and the byte count reported.

Subtree control writes report invalid argument for malformed tokens, missing device for a dead group, missing entry when enabling a controller absent from effective control, and busy when disabling a controller still enabled in a child. Success returns the input byte count rather than zero.

Conversion to threaded mode requires the main mutex, is a no operation when already threaded, refuses populated groups or groups with domain controllers enabled, requires a valid parent domain that can serve as a thread root, joins the parent domain for the group and its threaded descendants after snapshotting control, applies control without expecting migrations, and on success increments the parent threaded child count before finalizing.

Type display reports threaded for threaded groups and domain invalid for invalid domains and domain threaded for thread roots and domain otherwise. Type update only accepts threaded, locks the live group with draining of dying states, delegates to threaded enablement, and reports the byte count on success while rejecting other words and dead groups.

Depth and descendant limit files display the word max when set to the largest integer and otherwise the decimal value, accept max or a numeric string on write, reject negative values with a range error and dead groups with missing entry, and store the new limit under a live lock without draining. The events file reports populated and frozen indicators as labeled integers.

Statistics display reports the live descendant count and dying descendant count together with per controller live and dying counts for version two bound controllers that are not inhibited. Live counts derive from subsystem state descendant tracking plus one for the group itself when present, and dying counts come from stored dying counters.
Control file vocabulary uses max for unlimited depth and descendant limits, and the events file uses populated and frozen as labels for its two integer lines.
Statistics vocabulary uses nr_descendants and nr_dying_descendants for group counts, with per controller lines prefixed by nr_subsys and nr_dying_subsys followed by the controller name.

Statistics collection runs under read copy update without full locking, so concurrent mutations can yield inconsistent snapshots. Only controllers bound to the default root and not inhibited are included, with others silently omitted.

Threaded conversion asserts holding of the main cgroup mutex. Type and subtree control updates lock the live kernfs node with draining enabled to retire dying states, while descendant and depth limit updates lock live without draining. All paths unlock the node before returning.
Open file private state for cgroup files contains a peak tracking subrecord. The accessor interprets the generic private pointer as that container and returns the address of its peak member.
Path display holds the css set spin lock with interrupts disabled across namespace group resolution and kernfs path rendering to stabilize the ancestor pointer during formatting.

Parameter identifier enumerations list one value per recognized mount word plus a trailing count for version two, and a single value for cpuset mode. They serve as internal dispatch tags between the parameter table and the parse switch.
